# COMMON SIGNAL

## Identity
- Project: COMMON SIGNAL
- Reception wall wording: COMMON SIGNAL
- Reception wall phrase: Room for remote voices
- Direction: retained oak furniture, cork flooring, wool-felt panels and a clay-coloured camera background

## Existing room

- Axes: x east, y north, z above finished floor
- Coordinate units: m
- Internal area: 96 m²
- Fixed elements: shell, entrance, windows, column, shaft, floor power points, east-wall power/data point and east-wall cable tray
- Permitted additions: lightweight internal partitions and cable branches

steps.userMessage:
COMMON SIGNAL | A hybrid office for a twelve-person design and technology team

We are adapting an existing office for COMMON SIGNAL. The clear room measures 12.0 m east–west by 8.0 m north–south, with a 3.2 m ceiling. Coordinates start at the southwest internal corner; x runs east and y runs north. The south entrance occupies x = 0.6–1.8 m, is 1.2 m wide and 2.2 m high, and opens inward on its west hinge. Two north windows occupy x = 1.0–4.0 m and x = 7.0–10.0 m; each has a 0.9 m sill and a 1.8 m opening height. A 0.4 m square column is centred at (6.0, 4.0) m. A service shaft occupies x = 11.4–12.0 m, y = 0.0–0.6 m. Retain this shell, both windows, the entrance, column, shaft, floor power points at (3.0, 5.0) m and (9.0, 5.0) m, and the east-wall power/data point at (12.0, 1.0) m, 0.3 m above the floor. The existing east-wall cable tray is 2.9 m above the floor. New lightweight partitions and cable branches can be added within the shell.

Our team has 12 members: 4 designers, 6 engineers and 2 delivery leads. Average attendance is 6; all 12 attend Tuesday workshops. Build around six retained desks and the existing furniture and meeting equipment recorded in the fact sheet. The arrangement needs Focus, Team Call, Solo Call, Discussion, Reception and Equipment zones. Two video meetings must run together while colleagues work at desks and two visitors arrive. Give camera backgrounds a deliberate material treatment and give visitors a route to Reception and Team Call separate from desk working space. The direction is already set: retained oak furniture, sealed cork flooring, wool-felt panels and a matte clay camera background in #B66F52. Print "COMMON SIGNAL" and "Room for remote voices" on the reception wall. Develop the functional and furniture schedule first, then carry its zone names, areas, quantities and material codes through the drawings.

Audience: our studio partners, workplace coordinator and fit-out contractor, for the layout decision, furniture allocation and installation brief.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the room coordinates, attendance records, furniture inventory, equipment dimensions, finishes and lighting requirements. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md contains the proportions, formats and stages of the 14 deliverable files. existing-office-constraints.png records the fixed shell, service points and movable equipment envelopes. retained-furniture-and-av.png records the appearance of our retained desk, chair and meeting equipment. workshop-attendance-reference.png provides the human context of a twelve-person workshop. remote-call-reference.png provides the human context of local and remote colleagues sharing a discussion.

Deliverables:
1. A functional and furniture schedule, one document, stating each zone's proposed net area, capacity, furniture and equipment quantities and dimensions, and the four finish codes; minimum areas of Focus 24 m², Team Call 12 m², Solo Call 4 m², Discussion 14 m², Reception 8 m² and Equipment 6 m²
2. One furnished plan with the six named zones and their areas, all inventory items, partition thicknesses, door swings, camera cones, visitor and staff routes, the narrowest clear passage and a 1500 mm turning circle at Reception
3. One reflected ceiling and services plan locating AC-01 panels, L-01 ambient lights, L-02 task lights and L-03 accent lights, their separate controls, and cable branches from the three existing service points and east-wall tray
4. Two dimensioned interior elevations, one of the north wall and one of the east wall, with floor, ceiling, window and equipment mounting heights and finish codes
5. One meeting-node sheet covering Team Call and Solo Call, with furniture dimensions, both screen assemblies, camera positions at 1200 mm above the floor, 90-degree horizontal camera cones, seated participants and PT-01 backgrounds
6. One equipment and storage detail sheet with the 12-compartment locker bank, separate technology cabinet, printer, router, charging positions and cable access
7. One materials and lighting board with FL-01 sealed cork flooring, WD-01 clear matte oak, AC-01 wool felt and PT-01 matte clay paint #B66F52, plus the types, positions and controls of L-01, L-02 and L-03
8. Two interior perspectives: C1 from (2.0, 1.0, 1.6) m towards (10.0, 6.0, 1.6) m, and C2 from (10.5, 6.5, 1.6) m towards (2.0, 2.0, 1.6) m, with both viewpoints located in clear circulation space
9. Two occupied-state views using C1: Tuesday Workshop with six people at Focus and six at Discussion; Wednesday Calls with two people at Focus, three local and five remote participants in Team Call, one local and one remote participant in Solo Call, and two visitors at Reception
10. One 10-second walkthrough connecting Reception, Focus and Team Call, using the developed layout and showing the reception wording and meeting equipment
11. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, opening with the chosen spatial arrangement and reusing the schedule, plans, elevations, meeting and storage details, materials, perspectives and both occupied states

Acceptance:
- The functional and furniture schedule, furnished plan and presentation repeat all six zone names, the same proposed net areas meeting the six stated minima, and the inventory quantities. The plan accounts for the full 96 m² as net zones, circulation, partitions, column and shaft, with a minimum 1200 mm clear main route and the 1500 mm Reception turning circle.
- The furnished plan, ceiling and services plan, two elevations, perspectives, occupied-state views and walkthrough retain the 12.0 × 8.0 m shell, 3.2 m height and all recorded fixed features. C1 and C2 match their stated coordinates and directions; the furniture and partitions occupy the same positions throughout.
- The meeting-node sheet, furnished plan and Wednesday Calls view show two simultaneous calls with the stated participant split, both 90-degree camera cones and both cameras at 1200 mm. Camera cones contain the seated local participants and terminate on PT-01 backgrounds; visitor circulation stays outside the cones and desk working envelopes.
- The storage detail and furnished plan contain six desks, one discussion table, one video table, one call shelf, 19 chairs, 12 locker compartments and one technology cabinet, with the dimensions in the fact sheet. The Tuesday Workshop and Wednesday Calls views contain respectively 12 and 8 physically present people in the named zones.
- The schedule, materials and lighting board, ceiling and services plan, elevations and presentation use the same four finish codes; the ceiling and services plan and materials board locate all three lighting layers and their separate controls. AC-01 appears above Focus and on the Team Call wall, and its code is legible in C2.
- C1, both occupied-state views, the walkthrough and presentation display COMMON SIGNAL and Room for remote voices on the reception wall. The walkthrough lasts 10 seconds, and the presentation contains at least 8 pages with the zone areas, furniture quantities and earlier drawings.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
